title: Air India Launches Mumbai-Toronto Nonstop, Adds 4,400 Monthly Seats on India-Canada Routes
excerpt: The seasonal service starting October 25 makes Air India the only carrier flying direct between Mumbai and Toronto, with premium capacity to the Canadian city rising 71 percent.
body:
• Air India will launch a seasonal nonstop Mumbai-Toronto service three times weekly from October 25, 2026, through March 26, 2027, becoming the only airline offering direct flights between the two cities.
  • The expansion adds approximately 4,400 seats per month between India and Canada, with premium seat capacity to Toronto increasing by 71 percent.
  • Upgraded Boeing 777-300ER aircraft will serve the route with eight First Class suites, 40 Business Class flat beds, 280 Economy seats, and onboard WiFi.
  • Air India is also deploying its new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on the Delhi-Toronto route, with all Toronto flights operating new or upgraded interiors from January 2027.

Air India has confirmed a new seasonal nonstop service between Mumbai and Toronto for the Winter 2026-27 schedule, making it the only airline in the world to fly direct between India's financial capital and Canada's largest city. The route launches October 25, 2026, and will operate three times weekly through March 26, 2027.

The airline said the expansion will add approximately 4,400 seats each month between India and Canada, while premium seat capacity to Toronto will rise by 71 percent. Air India will operate 20 weekly flights between the two countries this winter: 10 from Delhi to Toronto, three from Mumbai to Toronto, and seven from Delhi to Vancouver.

Route Details and Schedule

Flight AI193 departs Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport at 4:00 a.m. and arrives at Toronto Pearson International Airport at 10:00 a.m. local time. The return, AI192, leaves Toronto at 12:30 p.m. and lands in Mumbai at 2:10 p.m. the following day. Flights operate every Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wE81aWMr9T8

The route covers approximately 7,775 miles, placing it among Air India's longest nonstop services. A two-and-a-half-hour turnaround at Toronto Pearson separates the outbound and return legs.

Upgraded Cabins and New Aircraft

The Mumbai-Toronto service will use upgraded Boeing 777-300ER aircraft featuring eight First Class suites with privacy sliding doors, 40 flat-bed Business Class seats, and 280 Economy seats. WiFi connectivity will be available onboard.

Separately, Air India has begun deploying its brand-new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on the Delhi-Toronto route, bringing its latest cabin products to Canada for the first time. Seven of the 10 weekly Delhi-Toronto flights will operate with the new aircraft this winter. The remaining three will transition from 777-300ERs to 787-9s from January 2027, at which point all Air India services to Toronto will feature new or significantly upgraded cabin interiors.

"Canada is one of Air India's most important international markets, with deep people-to-people connections driving strong demand for travel, particularly during the festive and holiday season."

— Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

Connecting Beyond Mumbai and Toronto

Passengers on the new route can connect through Air India's hubs in Mumbai and Delhi to destinations including Ahmedabad, Amritsar, Bengaluru, Chandigarh, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kochi, Ludhiana, and Vadodara. For the large Gujarati, Punjabi, and South Indian communities in the Greater Toronto Area, the connections remove the need for a Delhi layover that has long been the default routing from western and southern India.

Why It Matters for the Diaspora

Canada is home to one of the world's largest Indian diaspora populations, with the Greater Toronto Area alone accounting for a significant share. The Mumbai-Toronto corridor has long been underserved by direct flights, forcing travelers to route through Delhi, the Gulf, or Europe. The seasonal timing — October through March — covers Diwali, Christmas, and the winter holiday period when diaspora travel demand peaks.

The move is part of Air India's broader turnaround under the Tata Group, which acquired the carrier in 2022. The airline has been investing heavily in fleet renewal and cabin upgrades as it works to reclaim market share on key international routes.

What's Next

Air India said it plans to evaluate the Mumbai-Toronto route's performance during its seasonal run to determine whether it will become year-round. The airline has also been restoring international routes that were cut during the pandemic, with most expected to resume by September 2026.
